chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ali ibn Hadid, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Khul' (wife-initiated divorce) is a final divorce and has no right of return. Zurarah said: It occurs only in the same manner as divorce, either when she is pure (from menses) or pregnant, with witnesses. The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: As for Al-Mubarat, it is a type of Khul' until the end of the chapter.
ai.seo_question: What are the legal conditions and nature of Khul' divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib establishes Khul' as a distinct, irrevocable divorce (Bain) where the husband relinquishes his right to take the wife back during the waiting period (Iddah), contrasting it with Talaq al-Raj'i. It further clarifies the procedural requirements, noting that like standard divorce, it necessitates the wife being in a state of purity (Taharah) and the presence of witnesses, a point emphasized by the narrator Zurarah. The text also categorizes Mubarat (mutual release) as a specific subtype of Khul', highlighting the flexibility in marital dissolution within Shia jurisprudence.
